page.title: Best Robot Lawn Mower with a Bag (2026): Picks Up Clippings and Leaves
page.h1: Best robot lawn mower with a bag
page.desc: Most robot mowers only mulch. The ANTHBOT N8 has a 23 L bag it empties by itself, rated for 0.37 acre. Test results on leaves and noise, plus what to buy if you don't need a bag.
page.intro:
Short answer. The best robot lawn mower with a bag is the ANTHBOT N8 ({buy:anthbot-n8}): a built-in 23 L (6.1 gal) bag that it empties by itself at a spot you set, on lawns up to 1,500 m² (0.37 acre). It does pick up leaves: in PCWorld's test it emptied the bag without a single failure, and Notebookcheck found it left only a few leaves behind. The trade-off is noise: about 68 to 70 dB at 3 ft while collecting, which Notebookcheck calls nearly as loud as a regular mower.

The only other bagging robot we found for US buyers is Mammotion's YUKA with its add-on Sweeper Kit. Mammotion rates the YUKA for just 18% (10°) slopes once the sweeper is on. The N8 is rated for 45% (24°), and Anthbot doesn't list a lower figure with the bag. On 2026-11-11 we found YUKA parts on Mammotion's US store but no listing for the mower itself.

If your trees drop only a light layer of leaves, you may not need a bag. The MOVA LiDAX Ultra 2000 ({buy:mova-lidax-ultra-2000}) mulches up to 0.5 acre using 3D LiDAR, with no RTK antenna. For a small, shaded yard, the ANTHBOT M5 LiDAR ({buy:anthbot-m5-lidar}) covers 0.12 acre without needing satellite signal.

page.after:
What owners and testers complain about

  • Noise while collecting (4 tests): the fan that pulls clippings into the bag is loud. Testers measured 68 to 70 dB on the N8 and almost 70 dB on the YUKA with its sweeper. For plain mowing, Anthbot rates the N8 at 58 dB.
  • Wet or matted leaves (4 sources): collection works best on dry leaves. Leaves packed down by rain still need a rake, and the YUKA sweeper needed several passes on wet clumps. Mulch-only robots don't clear leaves at all.
  • Edges and turning room (4 sources): the N8 is about 3 ft long. Testers saw uncut strips up to about 6 in along edges, and it needs room near the dock and the dump spot.
  • Rain in the bag (3 tests): water pools on the N8's bag cover if it rains while the mower sits at the dock.
  • 4G fees (3 reviews): cellular service is free for a trial, then it's a paid yearly plan. You only need it where your RTK antenna can't see the sky or Wi-Fi doesn't reach.
  • Support: on one page of Anthbot's Trustpilot reviews, 13 of 23 complained of slow replies or slow refunds and replacements. Buy from a seller with a clear return window.

Which one by need

  • Trees that drop leaves, or you hate clippings on the grass: ANTHBOT N8. It's the only built-in bag we found, and it's rated for 45% slopes.
  • Bigger lawn, light leaf fall, quieter mulching: MOVA LiDAX Ultra 2000. It covers 0.5 acre and needs no RTK antenna.
  • Small yard under heavy tree cover: ANTHBOT M5 LiDAR. LiDAR doesn't need a clear view of the sky.

Not recommended

  • A mulch-only robot if you get a thick fall leaf layer. It will chop leaves at grass height, but it won't clear them.
  • The YUKA with its sweeper on slopes steeper than 10°.
  • Any bagging robot if quiet night mowing matters. Mow without the bag or pick a mulching model.

notes: Query choice: 'robot lawn mower with bag' and the variants return thin results: maker blogs (Navimow, eufy, Anker, FJD) saying robots mulch, plus single-product reviews. There is no real roundup, so ANTHBOT's N8 owns a real niche. Pain points, by number of sources: loud while collecting, 4 (PCWorld just under 68 dB at 3.28 ft; Notebookcheck about 70 dB at 1 m; GSMGoTech about 70 dB, which looks like a rewrite of Notebookcheck; Notebookcheck almost 70 dB for the YUKA with sweeper). Wet or matted leaves, 4 (House Digest; an r/automower comment seen in a search snippet; a YUKA wet-clump review; therobotmower says mulchers don't clear leaves). Edges and turning room, 4 (PCWorld up to about 6 in uncut; Notebookcheck; GSMGoTech; House Digest). Rain pooling in the bag, 3. 4G fee after the trial, 3 (PCWorld says N8 4G is free 1 year then $35.99/yr; Freshly Charged says 3 months free; Notebookcheck says the M9 gets 3 months then about $40/yr; these conflict, so no figure is on the page). Manual mapping, 2. Anthbot support: on Trustpilot CA page 3, 13 of 23 reviews were negative about support or refunds, 8 mentioned hardware failures, and none mentioned N8 bag performance. YUKA owner on r/SegwayNavimow (snippet only): unstable firmware, defective first sweeper, flimsy bag. Segments and winners: (1) leaf or clipping pickup: ANTHBOT N8, deciding fact a built-in 23 L self-emptying bag with a 45% slope rating against the YUKA's 10° with sweeper (Mammotion support spec page, read directly); (2) larger lawn with light leaves: MOVA LiDAX Ultra 2000, $1,099 on us.mova.tech today, 0.5 acre, 3D LiDAR, no RTK, 45% (store text read 2026-11-11); (3) small shaded yard: ANTHBOT M5 LiDAR, $759. Verified 2026-11-11 with storecheck search on anthbot.com, read twice: N8 $1,359 (compare-at $1,699), available; M5 LiDAR $759 (compare-at $1,148), available; also M5 $549 and M9 $649, not recorded. storecheck product (variants) and WebFetch of anthbot.com returned HTTP 429 all session, including a final retry after a 4-minute wait, so variants, warranty, return policy and any homepage banner code are NOT verified. The warranty and returns fields say so. T3's US page reportedly lists 3 years on the machine and 2 on the battery, but that came from a search snippet only and is kept off the page. Codes: the network gave none. I couldn't load anthbot.com's banner or product page because of the 429s, and the store search text showed no code. A Slickdeals code (ANNIVDEAL50) was left out on purpose because it comes from a coupon site. Unverified and kept off the page: N8 slope with the bag fitted (Anthbot gives only 45%); the YUKA bag size (22 L in snippets only); the YUKA US price (the Mammotion US store search showed YUKA parts but no YUKA mower or sweeper kit listing, and the sweeper product page returned 429); the 99% collection rate (maker claim); N8 runtime (Freshly Charged says about 90 minutes; GSMGoTech says about 2 hours). M5 LiDAR specs (20 cm width, 40-minute runtime, IPX6) come from the Easy Lawn Mowing review, not the store page. No Amazon records, per the temporary rule.
